leftEvidence.title: An everlasting covenant recalls mercies to David

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The thirsty are invited without price, hear a call to listen and live, receive language of everlasting covenant and David’s sure mercies, and are summoned into a widening relation with nations.
points.right: The promised days bring a righteous Branch, saved Judah, secure Jerusalem, continuing Davidic rule and priestly service, and a covenant comparison with day and night.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Davidic mercies are placed within invitation and international reach inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Davidic and priestly continuity are defended through creation-order language inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Isaiah 55:1–5 and Jeremiah 33:14–26 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Branch, throne, priests, and creation order are bound together

payload.tension: Isaiah 55:1–5 foregrounds Davidic mercies are placed within invitation and international reach; Jeremiah 33:14–26 foregrounds Davidic and priestly continuity are defended through creation-order language. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
